hints.content:
The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$ and intersects its midline at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/045d194412b500fdd873c28902f2f903.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\blue{4\cos(0.25x-0.25\pi)-3}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\cos(x)}$ to $\green{\cos(0.25x)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{0.25}=4$, so the intersection point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $2\pi$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\cos(0.25x)}$ to $\red{4\cos(0.25x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $4$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $4$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point at (two pi, zero).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, one) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point at (two pi, zero). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at a maximum at (zero, four) and a point at the midline next to the mentioned point at (two pi, zero).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{4\cos(0.25x)}$ to $\blue{4\cos(0.25x-0.25\pi)-3}$, which is equivalent to $4\cos{\large(}0.25(x-\pi){\large)}-3$, is a translation to the right by $\pi$ units and a translation downwards by $3$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the maximum point is now at $\left(\pi,1\right)$ and the intersection with the midline is at $(3\pi,-3)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at a maximum at (pi, one) and a point on the midline next to the mentioned point at (three pi, negative three).
